section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Functional Body Appreciation Scale (FBApS), an instrument developed (via qualitative interviews with first-time pregnant women) to measure appreciation of body functionality; five items were used with responses on a 5-point Likert scale and higher scores indicate greater appreciation. The original validation reported Cronbach's alpha = 0.82 and the present study reported internal consistency α = 0.70. The section notes correlations with body surveillance, depressive symptoms, and less healthy prenatal behaviors but provides no information on sample size, demographics, BMI assessment, survey method, country, or number of studies.
section_summary.evidence_source: The Functional Body Appreciation Scale (FBApS; Rubin & Steinberg, 2011) is one of two domains of an 11-item measure of body functionality... Responses were rated using a 5-point Likert scale, ranging from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree)... Cronbach's alpha coefficient was 0.82 in the original validation sample (Rubin & Steinberg, 2011). Internal consistency in the present study was acceptable (α = 0.70). In terms of further validity indices, correlational analyses revealed a significant negative association with body surveillance, depressive symptoms and engagement in less healthy prenatal behaviors (Rubin & Steinberg, 2011).
